items.text: Dalgha Khatinoglu stated that the reduction in Iran's oil loading does not necessarily mean a reduction in exports, as some oil remains in southern Iranian waters due to the US naval blockade. She added that despite oil exports last year, the Islamic Republic faced a currency shortage. Now, with a sharp decline in oil sales and near halt in petroleum product exports, sustaining this situation is difficult.

A video shows that Iranians in Germany held a rally in Dusseldorf on Friday. The gathering was in support of the national revolution and against executions. This event was reported by Iran International.

Ahmad Alavi stated that the Islamic Republic is trapped in a decision paralysis due to corruption, resource shortages, and internal divisions. He said that rising prices could intensify protests. Suppressing protests may deepen divisions within the government.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated at the 'Industry, Mining, and Green Services' conference that the government alone cannot address environmental issues. He emphasized that protecting the environment is a shared responsibility among the government, industry, and the people. These remarks came amid increasing criticism of Iran's environmental policies.

The number of executed prisoners in Isfahan's Dastgerd prison has increased to four. These executions took place in the early hours of Wednesday, August 19. A detailed report on this incident has been published.

Some NATO member countries are considering options to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. This action will not be within the framework of an official NATO mission. Military commanders have discussed possible participation in a virtual meeting.

Mohammad Reza Aref emphasized the need to reform the energy consumption pattern, stating that part of the country's income is spent on gasoline, which imposes pressures on other sectors. He pointed out the difference in fuel consumption between income deciles, noting that the richest decile consumes about 23 to 24 times more than the poorest. Aref linked the opposition of low-income groups to gasoline price increases to their reaction to changes in energy policies.

Iranians in Germany gathered on Friday in front of the Islamic Republic consulate in Munich. The protest was held to oppose executions and repression in Iran. A video of the gathering was sent to Iran International.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said that if unprecedented US sanctions coincide with a large-scale war, the resilience of the Islamic Republic cannot be maintained. He identified the main issue as the fragility of the government.

The regulation for controlled cultivation of Shaqayeq Elifra and the industrial hemp cultivation guideline in Iran have been announced. Cultivation will be supervised and conducted according to the Ministry of Health and Agriculture's regulations. The allowed THC content level defines the legal boundary for hemp cultivation.

The head of nomadic affairs in Semirom reported a shortage of health facilities and difficulties in accessing medical centers for nomads. Drying springs and drinking water supply problems were also mentioned. The possible link between some nomads' health issues and drinking water is under investigation.

Three detainees from the December 2025 protests, Mohammadreza Majidi-Asl, Behrouz Zamani-Nejad, and Kourosh Zamani-Nejad, were transferred from Tehran Grand Prison to Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. The transfer took place on Saturday, August 31. The reason for the transfer is unknown.

The deputy of human resources planning in Kerman's education department announced a shortage of 4,400 teachers for the new school year. Reasons include imbalance between incoming staff and retirements, cancellation of recruitment exams, and lack of soldier-teacher recruitment. Previously, the shortage was reported as 3,000 teachers.

The Public Duty Organization denied rumors about football players serving their military duty in non-military Premier League teams. All athlete conscripts must serve in military sports teams. Alireza Beiranvand will have to serve his military duty in military teams starting from Mehr 1405.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei mentioned the existence of an "octopus" in the automotive industry. He stated that until this "octopus" is removed, the condition and quality of cars will remain the same. These remarks point to structural problems in the automotive industry.

A citizen in Markazi province stated that some people have been forced to steal electric cables due to poverty. This issue was explained in a video sent by him. The incident occurred in neighborhoods of Markazi province.

Reports have emerged about a possible Iranian attack on US positions in Bulgaria. NATO has assured Bulgaria it is ready to defend in case of an attack. Requests have been made to hold a security meeting with the Bulgarian president.

Kayhan newspaper, responding to Ahmad Abedini's criticism, stated that hijab is a necessity of Islam and not a marginal issue. The paper called linking mandatory hijab to economic problems an evasion of religious responsibility. Kayhan emphasized that the government's duty is not only to provide livelihood but also to facilitate the implementation of religious laws.

The street performance of women with optional hijab in Ekbatan has received widespread attention on social media. One user described this movement as the victory of Iranian women against the Islamic Republic. More details are provided in an interview with Ayah Deris.

Farzaneh Fasihi, an Iranian Olympic runner, announced that despite qualifying, she was not allowed to register for the World Championships. She stated that she has been under pressure and was deprived of her basic athlete rights. Fasihi has faced pressure due to her protests against the killings by the Islamic Republic.

Arash Emamjomeh, a citizen from Saqez, was arrested by security forces on Friday, August 14. Nine days after his arrest, there is still no information about his whereabouts or condition. This situation has caused concern.

A video circulated on social media shows Basij forces placing children behind heavy military vehicles. This act is part of the ongoing securitization of the environment. The use of children in military settings has been highlighted.

Kamran Mirhaji, the prosecutor of Fars province, announced that organizers of unauthorized or non-compliant celebrations will be prosecuted. Cafes, halls, and venues hosting such events may be closed. Additionally, related virtual pages and channels will be blocked.

Hossein Taeb warned about the possibility of resuming negotiations and said the Iranian people should not be deceived by the apparent return to talks. He added that the enemy did not fulfill its commitments in the agreement and continued to break promises and apply pressure. These remarks were made at a ceremony honoring mosque activists.

The football360 website owned by Adel Ferdosipour has become accessible again after more than a month of suspension. The site and app were suddenly taken down a month ago, which some linked to Amir Ghalenoei's protests. The national team and related media denied this connection, but Tasnim news agency stated the filtering was due to an interview with Alireza Faghani.

According to a report by Kepler, Iran's oil loading has decreased to 156,000 barrels per day. This amount is about one-tenth of the pre-war level and has made Iran's oil exports disastrous. Continued restrictions may lead to reduced production and long-term damage to oil wells.
A man in Tehran was arrested on charges of assaulting a young woman. After the woman's complaint and the man's confession, he was sent to prison. The case is under judicial authority.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin stated that Trump believes the US will achieve its goals in nuclear, proxy, and missile areas with or without an agreement. He added that the Islamic Republic has become weak in nuclear and proxy areas. Additionally, society no longer equates the Islamic Republic with Iran, indicating the government has lost national authority.

92 percent of participants in the Iran International survey said they do not want to marry or have children due to poverty, insecurity, and an uncertain future. More than 10,000 people participated in this survey. Further details were provided in an interview with Mohsen Mahimini.

A video shows the wife of the missing person Ali Khosravi taking their young child and the deceased wife to his grave. Ali Khosravi was killed by officers on January 8 in Shahin Shahr. His child was born six months after his death.

Asieh Amini stated that the widespread presence of women without mandatory hijab indicates that people have gained the upper hand in the confrontation with the Islamic Republic. She added that the government still holds the law, budget, and tools of repression. This analysis reflects the social situation of women and society.

Participants in a protest rally in Stockholm stated they have not left the streets for eight months. They said they will hold the Lion and Sun flag until Reza Pahlavi calls for action. They also emphasized continuing the path of the families of the disappeared until the fall of the Islamic Republic.

Al Wasl Club of the UAE announced that Mehdi Taremi has joined the team. After years of playing in European football, Taremi has returned to Asian football. Al Wasl will face Shabab Al Ahli in the third week of the UAE league, where Sardar Azmoun and Saeed Ezatolahi play.

Prolonged drought and unprecedented heat have lowered the water levels of the largest reservoirs in the US. Lake Mead has reached its lowest level, and Lake Powell holds only 22% of its water. This situation serves as a warning of the climate crisis in the US.

Arsalan Yazdani, a Bahá'í citizen, was arrested by security forces in Tehran and transferred to an unknown location. His arrest took place on Saturday, 31 Mordad. Some of his personal belongings, including his mobile phone and laptop, were confiscated.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, visited the underground missile production site of the defense industries. He stated that the Ministry of Defense has produced equipment with better quality and quantity. He also emphasized that the enemy cannot fight against the will of the Iranian nation.

Reza Sepahvand, spokesperson for the Energy Commission of the Parliament, confirmed the use of methanol in gasoline blends and stated that the methanol content is about half a percent. He added that this amount does not cause problems for vehicles and claims of damage to car parts are unfounded.

Citizens have installed a joint poster of Prince Reza Pahlavi and his daughter Noor Pahlavi on a street in Tehran. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. The action was reported in Tehran.
Dust storms on the route from Zabol to Zahedan have created a critical situation. Visibility on this route has significantly decreased. This condition has made travel difficult.

Ahmad Vahidi, the commander of the IRGC, expressed support for the approach of IRIB and praised its role in the recent war. He described IRIB's performance as valuable in documenting the war's epic and strengthening the Islamic Revolution's media front. This comes after prior criticisms of IRIB's performance by Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Masoud Pezeshkian.

Arzoo Keshvar, owner of a beauty salon in Isfahan, has been sentenced to 12 years in prison on charges of communicating with hostile states. She has been held in Dolatabad prison since last February. After her arrest, she was kept in solitary confinement and subjected to lengthy interrogations.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that messages have been received from neighboring countries regarding new security arrangements and economic cooperation. He accused the US of threatening regional security for Israel's benefit and emphasized the need for a local and independent order. Additionally, the UAE has suspended its commercial activities with Iran until further notice.

Farzaneh Fasihi, an Iranian Olympic runner, stated that she was threatened after protesting the killing of demonstrators in December 2025 and that officials prevented her from participating in the World Championships. She said she was the only Iranian athlete who qualified for the World Championships but was not registered. Fasihi has started legal proceedings to pursue her rights.

In the ninth month of weekly gatherings of Iranians in Stockholm, participants emphasized continuing street presence until the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. Political activists and a performance group called for the closure of the Islamic Republic's embassy in Sweden. The gathering was held to support the people of Iran.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, visited an underground ballistic missile production facility. He was informed about the latest status of indigenous weapons production. Abdollahi emphasized that the enemy cannot fight against the will of the Iranian nation.

Behrouz Safari, head of the Tehran Travel Agencies Association, announced the closure of a large part of travel agencies. The recent war and its consequences have caused nearly two trillion tomans in damages to these offices. Severe market recession and wartime conditions have reduced travel and halted many agencies' activities.

Iranians in Germany held a rally on Saturday in support of the national revolution and against executions by the Islamic Republic in Cologne. This rally was reported through a video received by Iran International.

Mehdi Moslehi, an oil market expert, warned about the low octane gasoline supplied at gas stations. He said using this gasoline can reduce car acceleration, trigger warning lights, and damage parts. This issue can cause serious harm to vehicles.

The sentences of three prisoners related to drug crimes were carried out in Sabzevar prison. These prisoners included Ali Afzali and two brothers named Mostafa and Javad Karabi. The HRANA news agency confirmed their identities.

The Minister of Energy announced that power outages this year are less than last year, but the electricity for agricultural wells was cut for 6 hours a few days ago and now for 8 hours per day. Farmers in Beyza County report their crops are drying up. This issue has raised concerns about electricity management and its impact on agriculture.

The Israeli army announced that Sharif Al-Hasanat, a battalion commander in the Deir al-Balah brigade of Hamas, was killed in an attack. Al-Hasanat was involved in rebuilding the underground network and attacks against Israel. The Israeli army stated that measures were taken to minimize civilian harm before the attack.

Barak Ravid, citing three American officials, reported that on Friday, August 21, about 40 tankers passed through the southern deep route of the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately 16 million barrels of oil were exported through the strait on that day. This information was published on the X network.

Nazar Amidi stated that Iraq will not allow its territory to be used for attacks on other countries. He emphasized that possession of weapons should only be by the government and according to the constitution. He also mentioned the economic and security impacts of the war on Iraq.

Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Sari, was arrested by intelligence officers. The officers entered her home without a judicial warrant and searched it. Personal and electronic items were confiscated from the residence.

Senior African football officials have contacted FIFA Secretary General Matthias Grafström to inquire about his potential candidacy against Gianni Infantino in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. Fifteen African federations may not support Infantino. Grafström has not yet taken a clear stance on running.

A citizen protests the poor living conditions by showing the empty refrigerator at home and says people are hungry. He addresses officials, urging them to help. This is a protest against the current economic situation.

Ebrahim Rezaei warned about the presence of American aircraft and refuelers in airports of Qatar, Kuwait, and the UAE, calling it a threat. He cautioned these countries not to complain later. Previously, Ali Abdollahi also warned about the armed forces' oversight of US military activities in the region.

Qalibaf warned that if the decline in GDP and hunger among the people continue, the Islamic Republic will not survive, coinciding with the announcement of the start of the US economic war against Iran. The US Treasury Secretary stated that the Trump administration's goal is to overthrow the Iranian regime. This report was prepared by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

Household purchasing power has sharply declined, increasing economic pressure on lower income groups. Masoumeh Taherkhani stated that the devaluation of ration cards and rising food prices have led many households to eliminate items or buy cheaper, lower-quality goods.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated that the government will not allow US economic terrorism to target economic stability and people's livelihoods. He added that the experience of the Islamic Revolution has shown that economic pressure cannot change the will of the Iranian people. Aref emphasized that these pressures will have the opposite effect.

Jaber Rajabi said that Arab countries' efforts to create alternative routes to the Strait of Hormuz will weaken the Islamic Republic's leverage. He added that Tehran's policies undermine Iran's strategic advantage and push regional countries to invest in alternative routes. The Islamic Republic's threats will not prevent these projects from being implemented.

Hossein Nouri Hamadani sent a message to Mohsen Rezaei emphasizing adherence to the leader's guidance and resilience against the enemy. He called for a firm response to any aggression and maintaining internal unity. Nouri Hamadani warned that the enemies of Islam and the revolution are striving to attack the Islamic Republic.

Lionel Messi was fined by the MLS for slapping the back of Quinn Sullivan during a 2-2 draw against Inter Miami. The fine amount was not disclosed. Ian Fry was also fined for an altercation with Sullivan.

Public relations activists protested the prison sentences of Hooman Memarpanahi, Ghazal Nahani, and Hiva Seifizadeh. These sentences are related to organizing a concert at Amarat Robro. They demanded a review of these sentences.

Amirhossein Abrosh, a 17-year-old teenager, was released from Mashhad's correctional center after posting a 10 billion toman bail. This occurred on Saturday, 31 Mordad. He was among those detained during the nationwide protests of December 2025.

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, stated that Israel does not seek to escalate tensions with Turkey but will not accept Turkish military bases in Syria. He prefers maintaining the status quo and a diplomatic solution. Sa'ar also referred to the Islamic Republic's influence in Lebanon and Gaza and said they do not want a similar situation with Turkey and Syria.

Donald Trump called the Strait of Hormuz American territory and emphasized the military option. Tehran condemned the US secondary sanctions. Disagreements in Iran over how to face US pressures have increased.

A video released by state media shows a group of black-clad chador-wearing women gathering on the shores of Miankaleh. The gathering was held to support mandatory hijab and increase pressure on the people. This event took place in northern Iran.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated that as long as he is prime minister, a Palestinian state controlled by Iran will not be established in Gaza or the West Bank. He also criticized the left-wing coalition with the Muslim Brotherhood. These remarks were published on X network.
Two workers were injured in an incident at the Sarmak Malayer mining company. They were transferred to the hospital for further treatment. The accident occurred during work.

The spokesperson of the Energy Commission of the Iranian Parliament stated that about half a percent of methanol is added to gasoline and claimed it does not harm vehicles. The First Deputy Minister of Oil confirmed that substandard gasoline is produced in Iran. An energy expert warned that the methanol in Iranian gasoline could seriously damage fuel systems and car engines.

Hassan Hemmatifar, the prosecutor of Mashhad, stated that deterrent action against those who deliberately promote nudity and immorality is necessary. Special branches have been assigned in the Mashhad prosecutor's office to handle these cases. Judicial support for enforcers of virtue and preventers of vice is guaranteed.

Hossein Ali Hajideligani stated that the Islamic Republic should ensure that the UAE provides its facilities to Iran for many years. He mentioned that the compensation for damages caused by the UAE might be at the cost of having the entire UAE territory under Iran's control for years. These remarks were made in the Islamic Consultative Assembly.

Donald Trump has threatened that any country trading with Iran will pay a heavy price. This report examines Iran's largest trading partners based on World Bank data. An interview with Mohammad Mashinchian discusses how much these partners will stand by Tehran.

Signs of internal disagreement within the Iranian government are observed. Pazyarian and Qalibaf call for an end to the war, while some military officials emphasize changing the military doctrine and preemptive attacks. This issue was discussed in an interview with Morad Vaisi.
On Wednesday, 28 Mordad, indiscriminate shooting by military forces occurred in Zahedan. This incident resulted in one citizen being injured. Further details are not available.

Niusha Saremi in the audio version of Titrawol referred to a verbal dispute between Iran and the United States. This dispute occurred on the eve of an economic war. New signs of division in Tehran have also been observed.

Axios reported that the amount of oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz has doubled with the creation of a US-protected shipping corridor. Omid Shukri, an energy market expert, predicted that if this trend continues and is confirmed, the supply of oil from Arab countries will increase, and global oil prices could decrease. He also added that the US has the necessary military capability to maintain this route, but this operation will incur significant costs for Washington, and insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz could increase oil transportation costs.

Masoud Pezeshkian spoke at Doctor's Day about the start of the war, saying it was believed that if the country's leaders were killed, the country would collapse. He added that Ali Khamenei declared the need to move beyond the status of neither war nor peace, and they will follow whatever policy the leadership sets. Pezeshkian also stated that the current agreement is the best agreement.

Mohsen Rezaee said that Mojtaba Khamenei, despite great sorrow, has managed the country powerfully and defended it in war. Rezaee added that Khamenei showed courage in diplomacy and war. He also noted that the leadership's decision to use experienced commanders means that experiences will be used in future battles.

Barak Ravid, Axios reporter, cited three US officials reporting that about 16 million barrels of oil passed through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz on Friday night. This report comes amid increased US economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. More details were provided by Samira Gharaei.

Mohsen Rezaee stated that Iran's defense strategies are evolving and diplomatic behavior needs reform after US breaches of trust. He said Iran today is different from the past and the image of the US has changed in the minds of the youth. Rezaee also mentioned transformations in war management, diplomacy, and political-social issues, emphasizing that the future war will be different.

Victor Montagliani, president of CONCACAF, has asked Gianni Infantino not to attend the under-14 Caribbean Football Union tournament. Montagliani believes the presence of the FIFA president will harm the event. However, Infantino has posted photos showing his attendance at the tournament.

Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, has not responded to questions following the disclosure of the $20 billion FFE plan. He also refused to answer questions from a Sky News reporter in Punta Cana. Infantino intends to run for a fourth term as FIFA president in the 2027 election.

Mohsen Rezaei warned that if neighboring countries join the economic war with the US, they will be considered enemies and their interests targeted. He stated that Iran does not seek to escalate the war but will respond strongly if neighbors side with the US. Rezaei also threatened to block oil exports from the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz.

Javad Khaki, a political prisoner in Karaj Central Prison, has been deprived of specialized medical treatment due to lung and intestinal infections. Prison authorities have denied his requests for leave and transfer to medical centers. His request for release with an electronic bracelet has also remained unanswered.

Ben Sabti said Israel targets any military equipment or advanced technology that threatens its military superiority. He added that Tel Aviv monitors and counters the activities of forces affiliated with the Islamic Republic and Hezbollah in southern Syria. He also mentioned disagreements between the US and Israel regarding Syria and Turkey and said that reducing tensions is possible by focusing on economic development.

Kevin Castro, former West Bromwich midfielder, died at the age of 25 during a friendly match in Portugal. He collapsed in the first half of the match against Estrela da Amadora in Lisbon. West Bromwich club will honor his memory in the next game.

The World Humanoid Robot Games began on Saturday, August 22, in Beijing. Robots competed in events such as 100-meter sprint, high jump, tennis, table tennis, and seven-a-side football. The five-day event continues until Wednesday, August 25, and includes competitions based on factory work and emergency response.

Washington Free Beacon reported that out of 209 journalists killed in Gaza, 120 had connections with Hamas and Islamic Jihad. This data was recorded by the Committee to Protect Journalists. The report was prepared by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Donald Trump is seeking to launch a new economic war and Iran will hold him even more accountable than the Sacred Defense. Citing a Financial Times report, he said the US waged this economic war against itself and Trump's policies have placed a heavy debt burden on the American people and its allies, pushing the 30-year US bond yield to its highest level in the 21st century.

Bayern Munich defeated Dortmund 2-1 to win the German Supercup for the twelfth time. The match was held at Signal Iduna Park, with goals from Braun and Ulises for Bayern. Since last season, the cup has been named the Franz Beckenbauer Cup.

The football teams Duhok and Talaba, coached by Yahya Golmohammadi and Alireza Mansourian, drew 3-3 in the second week of the Iraqi league. Duhok reached 2 points and Talaba earned their first point of the season.

Dozens of young people aged 18 to 25 have been arrested in Khuzestan on charges of espionage and connections with Israel. Some were sentenced to heavy prison terms in brief court sessions. Journalist Roghieh Rezaei says the government is using the wartime atmosphere to intensify internal repression.

Donald Trump, by posting on Truth Social, emphasized the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz with American forces escort. He reposted a piece by American commentator Marc Thiessen, which pointed to statistics of over 1,000 ships exiting the Strait of Hormuz with American forces escort.

Hackers affiliated with the Islamic Republic disrupted a UK power plant for four days last month. The power plant was relatively small and the disruption did not affect the wider electricity network. This incident coincided with cyberattacks on US water infrastructure.

Donald Trump reshared a tweet by Mark Tyson about escorting over a thousand ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The New York Post reported that the US has been assisting ships in passing through the strait since May. CNN stated that the operation mostly involved guiding ships rather than a conventional military escort.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that any country cooperating with the US to impose economic restrictions on Iran will be considered an enemy and targeted. He also threatened that if the new US plan is implemented, Iran will not allow any oil to leave the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. These remarks were made in response to the new US sanctions.

The Chilean Foreign Ministry announced that the activity of its embassy in Tehran will end on the 31st of August. The decision was made due to organizational review and to ensure the security of diplomats. After the embassy closure, consular services will be provided through the Chilean consulate in Ankara.

Reuters reported that Iran's economy is under severe sanctions pressure, and new US sanctions could increase this pressure. These measures are significant due to their potential impact on Iran's main trading partners, especially China, which buys over 80% of Iran's exported oil. Reuters also assessed that Iran still possesses sufficient missile and drone capabilities to disrupt oil tanker traffic and attack regional rivals.

The Iran Chamber of Commerce Research Center reported that the 12-day war, the Dey uprising and internet shutdown, and the 40-day war have delivered three heavy shocks to Iran's labor market. A significant number of jobs have been lost, and many medium-sized businesses have become small enterprises. This trend indicates a gradual decline in jobs and increased pressure on people's livelihoods.

Kayhan newspaper criticized statements by Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, calling them signals of weakness to the enemy. The paper described the dichotomies of "war-negotiation" and "livelihood-missile" as fabricated and emphasized that the solution to economic problems is effort and prudence. Kayhan added that overcoming the current situation must be through dignity and prudence, not passivity and compromise.

The execution of Majid Adineh, a detained protester from December 2025, has been carried out. He was accused of cooperating with Israel and the United States against national security. He was arrested on the evening of January 9, 2026, in Mohammadshahr, Karaj.

Hossein Ghazian referred to the Iran International survey results where over 92% of participants expressed reluctance toward marriage or having children. He noted that concern and uncertainty about the future is a significant point in the survey. This issue has also appeared in previous reputable surveys.

The New York Post reported that ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has nearly quadrupled in the past two weeks. This increase coincides with US efforts to create a safe shipping route near Omani waters.

Reza Goharzad, a journalist and political analyst, said the criticism by Kayhan newspaper of remarks by Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, describing them as "signals of weakness and passivity to the enemy," reflects a division within the Islamic Republic over continuing confrontation or moving toward negotiations. He added that increased US pressure on China could force Beijing to pressure Tehran to return to talks.

The Esteghlal and Sepahan clubs released a joint poster for their match. The game will take place on Sunday, August 23, 2026, during the third week of the Premier League. The match has been titled "Superclasico."

Luiz Hamariren, head of the youth branch of the Swedish Christian Democratic Party, said at a gathering of Iranians in Stockholm that the party demands the closure of the Islamic Republic's embassy in Stockholm. He added that the world must act to support the Iranian people and their freedom. The gathering involved discussions and slogans about regime change.

The monthly report for Mordad 1405 highlights human rights violations in Iran. It mentions executions without fair trials, suppression of freedom of expression, violence against women, and labor rights violations. The number of violations across the country is alarming.

The price of the US dollar in Iran's open market reached 197,500 tomans, setting a new record. The British pound surpassed 269,000 tomans and the euro approached 230,000 tomans. The price of a new design gold coin reached 214 million tomans.

Elnaz Rekabi reacted to Farzaneh Fasihi's removal from the Iranian national athletics team, emphasizing freedom. Farzaneh Fasihi stated she has been under security pressures and was prevented from registering for the World Championships. Despite threats, she said she continues her efforts.
